question.prompt: Which of the following expressions is never a prime number when \(p\) is a prime number?

solutions.title: Check divisibility by three
solutions.explanation:
Because \(26\) leaves remainder \(2\) when divided by \(3\), it is useful to check whether \(p^2+26\) is divisible by \(3\).

First, if \(p=3\), then
\[
p^2+26=9+26=35=5\cdot7,
\]
which is composite.

If \(p\) is any other prime, it is not divisible by \(3\), so \(p=3k+1\) or \(p=3k-1\) for some positive integer \(k\). In either case,
\[
p^2+26=(3k\pm1)^2+26
=9k^2\pm6k+27
=3(3k^2\pm2k+9).
\]
This is a multiple of \(3\) greater than \(3\), so it is composite. Hence choice C never gives a prime.

Each other expression can give a prime:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{A:}\quad 5^2+16&=41,\\
\text{B:}\quad 7^2+24&=73,\\
\text{D:}\quad 5^2+46&=71,\\
\text{E:}\quad 19^2+96&=457.
\end{aligned}
\]
These results are prime. For the largest one, \(\sqrt{457}<22\), and none of the primes \(2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19\) divides \(457\).

The answer is \(\boxed{p^2+26}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
